correctness.rationale: Exactly derived Gaussian sensor covariance and integral cross-covariances yield an explicit captured-variance formula. The strict derivative sign identity proves global high-budget midpoint optimality using a uniformly subunit compact ratio. Uniform first-order convergence plus strict corner derivatives proves exact endpoint-gradient optimality for sufficiently small precision at lambda=8. The intermediate-budget mixed witness defeats every pure mode by two positive exact rational inequalities. All scopes, limits and zero-precision conventions are stated. The standalone reproducer checks integrals, formula consistency and strict rational margins.

value.rationale: For gradient-enhanced probabilistic numerical integration, a fixed resource budget must be allocated between signal and slope observations. The finding proves the genuinely mixed mode is sometimes strictly necessary, not just permitted, while both extreme allocation modes are exactly optimal at other budgets. This identifies a non-obvious structural boundary to an often-implicit all-or-nothing heuristic. It needs neither a general paper-sized theorem nor exact intermediate phase boundaries, and the fixed absolute-noise precision model is materially motivated and explicitly identified.
